newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma bombing trial jury selection nearing end.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma bombing trial jury selection nearing end.

text.p: Jury selection in the Oklahoma City bombing trial is nearing an end, the presiding judge said Monday, setting the stage for opening statements to begin, possibly Thursday.

"We're getting closer here in terms of who is coming back to visit us. We won't keep you in suspense much longer," U.S. District Court Judge Richard Matsch told the 93rd prospective juror to be questioned. He told the candidate, who spent seven years in the Air Force, the court would tell him by early Tuesday whether he would be asked to serve on the jury.

Sources close to the case expect opening statements to begin Thursday, a day after defendant Timothy McVeigh turns 29. Since the trial began March 31 the judge, prosecutors and defence attorneys have been quizzing potential jurors to select a jury of 12 plus six alternates.

McVeight, a Gulf War veteran, is charged with bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City on April 19, 1995. The bombing -- the worst attack on civilians ever on U.S. soil -- killed 168 people, including 19 children.
McVeigh, who has paid close attention during juror questioning, has pleaded not guilty. He faces the death penalty if convicted.

Prospective jurors are being asked a range of questions to probe their opinions on the death penalty and to ascertain how much they have been exposed to news accounts of the case. Six have been excused publicly, including two who disobeyed the judge's orders about avoiding news on the case.
Matsch has not announced how many others have been dismissed for causes such as total opposition to the death penalty.
